name: HarmBench
intro: HarmBench 是一个标准化自动红队评测框架，包含 510 个由作者依据主流模型使用政策人工设计和反复筛选的有害行为，覆盖 4 个功能类别与 7 个语义类别。它通过固定的验证/测试划分、标准化生成设置和两类专用分类器，以攻击成功率衡量红队方法对目标模型及防御的突破效果。
org: Center for AI Safety, University of California Berkeley, Stanford University, University of Illinois
build_method: 政策提炼, 专家人工构建, 反复筛选, 分层划分
task_type: 自动红队, 安全测试
eval_feature: 对抗性, 保留测试集, 专用分类器
build_method_en: Policy Distillation, Expert Authoring, Iterative Curation, Stratified Splitting
eval_feature_en: Adversarial, Held-out Test Set, Specialized Classifiers
intro_en: HarmBench is a standardized automated red-teaming framework with 510 harmful behaviors manually designed and repeatedly curated by the authors from major model-use policies. The behaviors cover four functional and seven semantic categories. A fixed validation/test split, standardized generation settings, and two specialized classifier paths measure attack success against target models and defenses.

drawio_review_note: Reviewed against arXiv:2402.04249v2, Section 4 and Appendix B.5, and official repository snapshot 8e1604d1171fe8a48d8febecd22f600e462bdcdd. The pinned data/behavior_datasets release contains 400 text behaviors and 110 multimodal behaviors; the text CSVs materialize 80 validation and 320 test behaviors, while the 110 multimodal behaviors are published as an all-set and there is no separate 20/90 multimodal CSV at this snapshot. The paper remains authoritative for the total 100 validation / 410 test split and prohibits tuning on test or semantically identical behaviors. Authors use GPT-4 to distill OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and Inflection acceptable-use policies, then manually curate and filter 510 behaviors across seven semantic and four functional categories. The paper standardizes N = 512 test cases per behavior; N is the test-case count, not the completion length. Target completions use greedy decoding. At the pinned repository snapshot, the repository default is max_new_tokens=256 in generate_completions.py; this CLI default is not the paper's N. Non-copyright completions use the open Llama 2 13B yes/no classifier; copyright completions use overlapping-chunk MinHash with Jaccard threshold greater than 0.6. Attack success rate is the fraction of successful test cases per behavior and is averaged for reporting.
